messages.content: Write a Python worker that pulls items off a queue.Queue in a thread and processes each with a callback. Around 50 lines.
This already exists (`queue_thread_worker.py`, 53 lines) and does exactly what you asked. I don't need to write a new one — want me to reuse this, or write a fresh variant elsewhere?
Add a clean shutdown on a sentinel value.

Already has it — the sentinel shutdown is already implemented: `_STOP` sentinel (line 11), `stop()` puts it on the queue and joins the thread (line 27-30), and `_run` checks for it and returns (line 36-37). Nothing to add here.
An exception in the callback currently kills the thread silently. Handle it.

output: This already handles it: `_run` wraps `self._callback(item)` in a try/except (lines 35-40) that logs the exception via `logger.exception` and continues the loop — a bad callback logs and moves to the next item instead of killing the thread. Nothing to change here either.
